briefs.title: Online payments at booking
briefs.decision: 2026-11-17 Build it now. Why: the M2 focus, and five pilots asked for it.
briefs.problem: Clients book and do not show up, and studios chase payment by bank transfer afterwards.
briefs.doneWhen: A client pays by card on the booking page, and the booking is confirmed only after the payment succeeds.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.markdown: - Clients book and do not show up, and studios chase payment by bank transfer afterwards.

sections.heading: Who and evidence
sections.markdown:
- Five of the eight pilot studios asked for payment at booking in the 2026-11-18 calls.
- Pilots that take a deposit report 4% no-shows against 11% for the rest (STRATEGY.md B1).

sections.heading: Original idea
sections.markdown: Take the full class price by card when the client books.

sections.heading: Proposal
sections.markdown:
- The booking page sends the client to the provider's hosted checkout.
- The provider's webhook confirms the booking; a failed payment frees the slot.
- The dashboard lists each payment beside its booking.

sections.heading: Alternatives considered
sections.markdown:
| Option | Effort | Benefit | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Do nothing | none | No work. | No-shows stay at 11%. |
| Deposit only | S | Cuts no-shows. | Studios still chase the rest. |
| **Full payment by hosted checkout (recommended)** | M | No card data on our servers; no-shows fall. | A 1.5% fee per booking. |

sections.heading: Challenges and answers
sections.markdown: - 2026-11-17. Claim: studios may refuse the card fee. Answer: A1 holds; all eight pilots accepted it (STRATEGY.md).

sections.heading: Ramifications
sections.markdown:
| Area | Effect | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data and migrations | A payments table keyed by booking. | Additive migration. |
| Security and privacy | No card data stored; the webhook needs signature checks. | Verify every webhook signature. |
| Performance | none found | |
| User experience | One extra step before the confirmation. | Hosted checkout keeps the studio's colours. |
| Operations and cost | 1.5% per booking. | Shown on the pricing page (R-010). |
| Maintenance | One provider SDK to keep current. | |
| Dependencies | Needs R-002; R-008 and R-016 wait on it. | |
| Reversibility | Payments can be switched off per studio. | |

adrs.title: Take payments with hosted checkout
adrs.context:
R-007 takes a card payment when a class is booked. Studios are small and
cannot carry the card-data compliance work of a payment form on our pages.
adrs.decision:
Send the client to the payment provider's hosted checkout page and record the
booking when its webhook confirms the payment.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hosted checkout | Least compliance scope; one redirect | Chosen |
| Embedded card form | Stays on our page; full compliance scope | Rejected |
| Pay at the studio | No build; no-shows are not charged | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- A booking is pending until the webhook arrives.
- R-016 retries a failed card payment through the same webhook.

adrs.title: Store class times in studio local time
adrs.context:
Every pilot studio was in one timezone, and the timetable is entered in
local time.
adrs.decision: Store each class's start as the studio's local date and time.
adrs.alternatives: Store UTC and convert on display: more work for one timezone.
adrs.consequences: - Confirmation emails print the stored time as it is.

adrs.title: Store class times in UTC
adrs.context:
R-011 shows each confirmation in the studio's timezone, and R-013 adds
studios with locations in more than one timezone. Local times stored by
ADR-002 are ambiguous across daylight-saving changes.
adrs.decision:
Store each class's start in UTC with the studio's IANA timezone name, and
convert to the studio's local time when it is shown.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UTC and the timezone name | One conversion on display | Chosen |
| Local time with an offset | Breaks for repeating classes across a daylight-saving change | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- A one-off migration converts the stored times with each studio's timezone.
- Every display path calls the same `formatClassTime` helper.

adrs.title: Sync calendars through webhooks
adrs.context:
R-012 keeps a studio's external calendar and its timetable in step both ways.
Polling every calendar every few minutes would exceed the providers' rate
limits once more than a few dozen studios connect.
adrs.decision:
Subscribe to each provider's change notifications and fetch only the changed
events; poll once a day to repair missed notifications.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Calendar provider
  participant S as Slotwise
  P->>S: change notification (channel, resource)
  S->>P: fetch events changed since the sync token
  P-->>S: changed events and the next sync token
  S->>S: update the timetable
```

A notification carries no event data, only what changed:

```json
{
  "channel": "studio-42-main",
  "resource": "calendars/primary/events",
  "state": "exists"
}
```
adrs.alternatives: Poll every calendar every five minutes: simpler, but hits rate limits.
adrs.consequences: - Each provider needs a public webhook endpoint.

adrs.title: Send emails through our own SMTP server
adrs.context:
R-003 sends booking confirmations. A small SMTP server was quick to set up
for the pilot.
adrs.decision: Send every confirmation through one SMTP server we run.
adrs.alternatives: An email delivery service: a monthly cost before the pilot proved demand.
adrs.consequences:
- We watch the server's sending reputation ourselves.
- 2026-11-12 Deprecated: confirmations moved to the email provider's API after messages from the server landed in spam.

adrs.title: Cache timetable pages at the edge
adrs.context:
Imported from the studio app's own ADR folder. A studio shares its public
timetable link on social media, and a busy post sends thousands of visits in
minutes to a page that changes only when a class is booked.

![The timetable is served from the edge cache and refreshed on each booking](timetable-cache.svg)
adrs.decision:
Serve public timetable pages from the CDN's edge cache for up to 60 seconds,
and purge a studio's pages when one of its classes is booked or changed, so
R-011 confirmations and the page agree.
adrs.consequences:
- A booking appears on the public page within one purge, not on the next
  visit's database read.
- `Cache-Control: s-maxage=60` is set on every timetable response.
